page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is a virtual machine instance designed for compute-oriented workloads requiring minimal memory overhead. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core via hyperthreading. Hardware cache structures include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache. Memory is allocated at 2.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPUs, requiring attached network storage for persistent disk operations. Supported instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES, and FMA.

Benchmark metrics place the instance in the lower percentiles across synthetic tests, driven by its 2-vCPU configuration derived from a single physical execution core. In CPU testing, it achieved 1399.29 in stress-ng single-core and 1841.88 in multi-core execution. Geekbench evaluation recorded 1111.0 for single-core and 1311.0 for multi-core performance. PassMark returned an overall CPU score of 2160.18 and a memory score of 917.26. Large block memory operations registered read speeds of 13.72 GB/sec and write speeds of 11.78 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 1.75 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.06 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given the 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and the absence of bundled local storage, the primary tradeoff centers on memory constraint. High-memory data processing, caching, and concurrent large container deployments will face memory saturation. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-2 provides dedicated core access with modern vector instruction sets without paying for unneeded memory capacity. Appropriate workloads include lightweight batch processing, basic CI/CD worker steps, microservices, small web server components, and compute tasks requiring AVX-512 instructions with low memory footprints.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is an entry-tier compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 2.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.8 GHz, the instance utilizes a single physical core with hyperthreading and includes support for AVX-512, AES, and FMA instructions. The machine provides no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network storage solutions. In benchmark testing, the n2-highcpu-2 recorded a single-core stress-ng score of 1399.29, a multi-core score of 1841.88, and a PassMark CPU score of 2160.18. Memory bandwidth measured 13.72 GB/sec for uncached read operations. The strict 1.0 GB per vCPU allocation creates an operational tradeoff that restricts memory-intensive applications. Consequently, this server profile is best matched to lightweight background jobs, basic CI/CD test runners, small web serving components, and utility microservices where CPU execution takes precedence over RAM capacity.
